questions_and_answers.question: What does the participle ending with ता/ते/ती without an auxiliary verb express?
Which sentence is an example of a past contrafactual statement?

answers.answer: मौसम अच्छा होता तो मैं जाता

questions_and_answers.question: How is the negative formed in a contrary-to-fact clause?
What does the sentence ‘अगर मैं आपकी जगह होता तो ऐसा न करता’ mean?

answers.answer: If I were you, I wouldn’t do that
If I were you, I would do it
If you were me, you wouldn’t do that

questions_and_answers.question: What is understood after the word ‘जगह’ in these constructions?
Which sentence expresses a future contingent meaning?

answers.answer: अगर मैं आपकी जगह होऊँ तो ऐसा न करूँ
अगर मैं आपकी जगह होता तो ऐसा न करता

questions_and_answers.question: In which case is the postposition ‘ने’ typically used?

answers.answer: When there is no direct object
When the direct object is stated

questions_and_answers.question: Which sentence omits the postposition ‘ने’ because there is no direct object?
What does ‘मैं जा सकती तो ज़रूर जाती’ convey?

answers.answer: If I can go, I will
If I could have gone, I certainly would have
I will go if you ask

questions_and_answers.question: Which of the following examples shows the use of ‘न’ in a negative contrary-to-fact clause?

answers.answer: आप गोश्त न खाते तो तन्दुरुस्त हो जाते

articles.text:
The participle ending in **ता, ते, ती** without any auxiliary verb gives a past, contrary-to-fact meaning. Such clauses express situations that did not happen but could have. For example:

• मौसम अच्छा होता तो मैं जाता — If the weather had been good, I would have gone.
• मैं जा सकती तो ज़रूर जाती — If I could have gone, I certainly would have.

In negative contrary-to-fact statements, **न** is usually used:

• आप गोश्त न खाते तो तन्दुरुस्त हो जाते — If you hadn’t eaten meat, you would have become healthy.

The construction also contrasts with a present contingent meaning:

• अगर मैं आपकी जगह होता तो ऐसा न करता — I wouldn’t have done it that way if I had been in your shoes.
• अगर मैं आपकी जगह होऊँ तो ऐसा न करूँ — I wouldn’t do that if I were you.

Here, **में** or **पर** is understood after **जगह**. Some verbs, particularly transitive ones like **बोला** (speak) and **खेला** (play), are sometimes used without the postposition **ने** when no direct object is stated. When the direct object is present, **ने** tends to be used:

• इन्होंने हिन्दी बोली — They spoke Hindi.
• ये बोले — They spoke.
• हमने टेनिस खेली — We played tennis.
• हम खेले — We played.
